clue.text: Brightly coloured hat? We hear you are wearing that

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are taken as letters that sound the same
a hat wears nothing, but whoever wears it is under it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat
two letters pronounced like the two words, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: Someone sniffy remarks that the gaudy hat you have on is rather loud.
explanation.walkthrough: U R goes under the LID, making LURID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurid describes colours that are glaring, vivid and unpleasantly bright.

clue.text: Group of dreamers tolerates us working

indicators.note: working suggests the letters being worked into a new shape

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A band of idle fantasists puts up with us while we work.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Odyssey the lotus-eaters ate a fruit that left them in dreamy forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-eaters are people who live in idle, dreamy indulgence, after Homer's forgetful islanders.

clue.text: Playing field a player's first to go back over

indicators.note: the first of a word is only its opening letter

blocks.note: the rec is short for recreation ground
taken as written
the opening letter of player

explanation.surface: A sportsman is first to return over the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back' is not a reversal here; it is part of the definition. The rec is the British name for a public playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to recapitulate, going over the main points again briefly.

clue.text: Sign in with teeth sadly amiss — to see the likes of us?

indicators.note: something amiss is out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dental practice's sign: book in when your teeth are in a bad way and come to see us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins the two parts of the fodder; its letters are not used. The 'us' speaking are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental hygienists clean and care for teeth, so they are the professionals patients with neglected mouths visit.

clue.text: Sound from above? This is missing below

indicators.note: the word just named is missing, so it is dropped from the word before it

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters that go missing
under means below

explanation.surface: A riddle about a noise from the heavens, with a hint that something underneath is lacking.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'This is missing' literally, as an instruction: the word 'is' drops out of 'This'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunder is the rumbling noise produced by lightning in storm clouds overhead.

clue.text: Rebuke coming from country bumpkin losing head, interrupting smart gent

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its opening letter
to interrupt is to break into, so these letters sit inside the other word

blocks.note: a toff is a smartly dressed upper-class man
a hick is a rustic, unsophisticated person

explanation.surface: A posh gentleman is rudely interrupted by a yokel and scolds him.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for a posh, well-dressed man.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is informal British for telling someone off, a mild reprimand.

clue.text: Without guidance, without merit, without knowledge

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first piece surrounds the second

blocks.note: unled means not led, lacking guidance
to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A list of three lacks, like a damning school report.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle 'without' is the old sense meaning outside: the word for unguided wraps around the verb for merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlearned means uneducated, lacking learning or knowledge.

clue.text: Unease that could be engendered by sitcom if rude

indicators.note: something engendered is created out of material, so the following letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A crude television comedy could leave viewers squirming.
explanation.definitionFit: Discomfiture is a feeling of embarrassment or disconcertment, an uneasy state of mind.

clue.text: Managing school and boosted by success

blocks.note: riding a horse is managing it
a high school is a type of school

explanation.surface: Someone running a school is doing very well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managing school' hints at a riding school, a manège, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding high is an idiom for being very successful and confident at the moment.

clue.text: Husband considered "never good"' in retrospect, showing a certain sort of fake concern

definitions.text: a certain sort of fake concern

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect suggests reading the whole string from its end

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
to see something a certain way is to consider it
ne'er is the poetic contraction of never
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A wife looks back and decides her husband was never any good, revealing a hollow show of caring.
explanation.walkthrough: H, SAW, NE'ER and G run backwards to give GREENWASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwash is a company's misleading show of environmental responsibility, a pretended ecological concern used for public relations.

clue.text: Non-English visitors — they may breeze in

indicators.note: non- means without, so the letter for the next word is taken away

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
guests are visitors

explanation.surface: Foreign house guests who drop in casually.
explanation.walkthrough: To breeze in means to arrive casually, as visitors do; here the definition is literal moving air.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusts are sudden rushes of wind, which can blow into a room through an open door.

clue.text: From collection of old politician, by chance not complete

indicators.note: a word that is not complete lacks its final letter

blocks.note: ex means former
Lib is short for a Liberal
a risk is a chance

explanation.surface: A book once owned by a retired politician turns up by luck, though incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Ex libris is Latin for 'from the books of', printed on bookplates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex libris means from the library of, marking a book as part of someone's collection.

clue.text: See old books with pleasant binding

indicators.note: binding wraps around something, so this word encloses the other

blocks.note: nice means pleasant
OT is the Old Testament, a set of old books

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at antique books with attractive covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Binding' sounds like bookbinding, which suits the surface, but it means wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, notice is a plain synonym meaning to observe or become aware of something with the eyes.

clue.text: Like position of sailor maybe, well away from port?

definitions.text: Like position of sailor maybe, well away from port?

blocks.clueFragment: Like position of sailor maybe, well away from port?
blocks.note: surface reading: a seaman far out at sea, a long way from harbour
setter's reading: port is the left side of the ship, so a point well away from it lies towards the centre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests a harbour; it is the left-hand side of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle of a ship, midway between bow and stern or between the sides.

clue.text: Why each dog must be trained — one included rules for walkers etc.

indicators.note: training reshapes behaviour, so the letters are put into a new order
included means put inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An explanation of why every dog needs obedience training, with rules for pedestrians.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highway Code is the official British rulebook for road users, pedestrians included.
explanation.definitionFit: The Highway Code sets out the rules for everyone using British roads: drivers, cyclists and pedestrians.

clue.text: Specialist element said to be backing police investigator

indicators.note: said tells us the element's name is only to be pronounced, not spelt

blocks.note: tec is short for detective
the metallic element nickel, spoken after the detective

explanation.surface: A chemistry note that some element is backing a detective's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' here means coming behind, not reversal: TEC followed by NICKEL, said aloud, sounds like TECHNICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical as an adjective means specialised, belonging to a particular field of expert knowledge or skill.

clue.text: Team falling apart? That's very funny

blocks.note: a side is a team
splitting means coming apart

explanation.surface: A squad disintegrates, and someone watching finds it hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something side-splitting makes you laugh so hard your sides ache, so it is hilarious.

clue.text: Singer thus embracing musical work took off

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap arms around, so this word encloses what follows

blocks.note: so means thus
op. is short for opus, a numbered musical work
to take off is to run away

explanation.surface: A vocalist clutches a score and rushes away.
explanation.walkthrough: SO embraces OP plus RAN: S(OPRAN)O.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest voice range, usually a woman or boy.

clue.text: Numbers in financial documents — one number therein multiplied by five

indicators.note: multiplying a Roman numeral changes it into a different numeral, which replaces it

blocks.note: accounts are financial records
the Roman numeral two hundred sitting inside the word
two hundred times five is a thousand, Roman M

explanation.walkthrough: CC (200) in ACCOUNTS becomes M (1,000), giving AMOUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amounts are quantities or sums, the totals or figures a set of numbers records.

clue.text: One that may go through wood in county with endless wonder

definitions.text: One that may go through wood

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county
awe is wonder

explanation.walkthrough: BUCKS plus AW(E). A bucksaw is a saw set in an H-shaped frame for cutting logs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucksaw is a framed saw for cutting firewood, so it is a tool that passes through timber.

clue.text: Total entertainment — everything being enjoyed by blondes?

annotation.answer: ALL THE FUN OF THE FAIR

blocks.note: first meaning: every amusement on offer, an idiom from the funfair
second meaning: fair can mean fair-haired, so the fun belongs to blondes

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'the fair' as fair-haired people rather than a funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every bit of the excitement and amusement a situation offers, like everything at a travelling funfair.

clue.text: Man is fat — very many years getting stuffed

indicators.note: something stuffed is filled, so the time period goes inside

blocks.note: lard is pig fat
an eon is an immensely long time

clue.text: Strange female, old, having time in office

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
O is the abbreviation for old
a reign is a monarch's period in power

explanation.surface: An odd elderly woman has served a term in some post.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean strange or unfamiliar, alien to one's experience.

clue.text: After victory you initially like a drink in the bar?

definitions.text: like a drink in the bar

indicators.note: initially points at only the starting letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: a win is a victory
the opening letter of you

clue.text: To have low opinion of modern technology? That matters not a bit!

blocks.clueFragment: To have low opinion of modern technology

explanation.walkthrough: IT is the usual abbreviation for information technology, so 'it' in the phrase becomes modern technology.

clue.text: Criminal ten gaoled, given a stretch

clue.text: Fierce folk, initially getting into rows

clue.text: Move your hips without hesitation — thanks to me?

definitions.text: Move your hips without hesitation — thanks to me?

clue.text: One sad little person, boy getting lost

blocks.note: wee is Scots for little
taken as written

clue.text: Agriculturists at the cutting edge who hope to do well from investments?

definitions.text: who hope to do well from investments

blocks.clueFragment: who hope to do well from investments
blocks.note: second meaning: owners of stock in a company

clue.text: Careless type in drive policeman caught out

clue.text: Outcast somewhat masculine, from what we hear
